title: Definition
body_md: A \textbf{Dirac-harmonic map} is a pair $(u,\Psi)$ solving the system (\ref{eq:euler_lagrange}). A Dirac-harmonic map $(u,\Psi)$ is said to be \textbf{uncoupled} if $\mathcal{R}(u,\Psi)\equiv 0$ and \textbf{coupled} otherwise.
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md: A periodic Dirac-geodesic $(\gamma, \Psi)$ is said to be \textbf{spin $\nu$} if $S^1$ is equipped with the spin $\nu$ structure.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: The previous definition uses $H^1(S^1,\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})$ for labelling Dirac-geodesics. A similar definition can be made for any spin domain $M$.

label: lemma:holonomy
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:holonomy}
		Let $(\gamma, \Psi)$ be a spin $
u$ Dirac-geodesic in $N$. Then the parallel transport satisfies $X(1) = (-1)^{2
u}X(0)$ and $Y(1) = (-1)^{2
u}Y(0)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: This follows from $X$ and $Y$ being parallel and the (anti)-periodic behaviour observed for the sections of $\Sigma_\nu S^1$.

label: prop:quantisation
title: Proposition
head: environment

label: eq:curv_relation
title: Proof
body_md:
By the unit-speed assumption on $\gamma:[0,\ell]\rightarrow N$ we know that $\dot\gamma, J \dot \gamma$ is an orthonormal frame along $\gamma$. In this frame we see $$ R(X,Y)\dot\gamma = (K_N\circ \gamma)(h(\dot \gamma, Y)X - h(\dot\gamma, X)Y) = - (K_N\circ \gamma)\omega(X,Y)J\dot\gamma = -(K_N\circ \gamma) \omega_{\Psi}J\dot\gamma $$ and combining with (\ref{eq:dirac_geo}) 
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:curv_relation}
		(k_g - (K_N\circ \gamma) \, \omega_\Psi)J\dot \gamma =0
		\end{equation}
		where $k_g = h(\nabla_{\dot \gamma}\dot \gamma, J\dot\gamma)$ is the geodesic curvature. Denote by $\theta$ the angle between $X$ and $\dot\gamma$ and recall the classical relation $\dot \theta = -k_g$. Now (a) follows by an application of Gauss-Bonnet
		$$
		2\pi \chi(N_\gamma) - \int_{N_\gamma}K_N\, dA =  \int_{\gamma}k_g \, dt = - \int_\gamma \dot\theta \, dt = \theta(0)-\theta(\ell)
		$$
		and the fact that $\theta(0)-\theta(\ell)\, \mathrm{mod}\,2\pi$ measures the holonomy around $\gamma$. (b) follows by
		$$
		\omega_\Psi \kappa L[\gamma] = \omega_\Psi\int_{\gamma}(K_N \circ \gamma)\,dt =\int_\gamma k_g \, dt = 2\pi \chi(N_\gamma)- \int_{N_\gamma}K_N\, dA.
		$$

label: prop:parallels_dirac_geo
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:parallels_dirac_geo}
		The separating parallel $t \mapsto (s_0,\tfrac{t}{r(s_0)})$ can be extended to a Dirac-geodesic if $\dot r(s_0) = k+\nu$ with $k+\nu$ determined by Proposition \ref{prop:quantisation} (b).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Recall that the Gaussian curvature of $N_\sigma$ is $K_N = -\frac{\ddot r}{r}$.
		By Equation \ref{eq:curv_relation} the Dirac-geodesic equations are $\nabla_{\dot \gamma}\dot \gamma - (K_N\circ \gamma) \, \omega_\Psi \, J \dot \gamma = 0 $ which in coordinates $(s,\theta)$ are
		$$
		\begin{cases}
			\ddot \gamma_1 -r\dot r (\dot\gamma_2)^2 - \omega_\Psi \,\ddot r \,\dot\gamma_2 &= 0\\
			\ddot \gamma_2 + 2 \frac{\dot r}{r} \dot \gamma_1\dot \gamma_2 + \omega_\Psi\,\frac{\ddot r}{r^2} \,\dot\gamma_1 &= 0
		\end{cases}
		$$
		
		Now consider a separating parallel $\gamma_{s_0} = (s_0, \frac{1}{r(s_0)}t)$ for which the second ODE vanishes and the first ODE rearranges to
		$$
		\frac{\dot r(s_0)}{r(s_0)} + \omega_\Psi \frac{\ddot r(s_0)}{r(s_0)}=0 \Leftrightarrow -\omega_\psi \ddot r(s_0) = \dot r(s_0)
		$$
		and by $L[\gamma_{s_0}] = 2\pi r(s_0)$ and Proposition \ref{prop:quantisation} (b) the constant becomes $\omega_{\Psi} = -\frac{k+\nu}{\ddot r(s_0)}$ where we used that the Gaussian curvature is the constant $-\frac{\ddot r(s_0)}{r(s_0)}$ along $\gamma_s$. Hence, we obtain
		$$
		k+\nu = \dot r(s_0)
		$$
		where $k + \nu$ is determined by the Euler characteristic and the total Gaussian curvature. Now, we can take any $X_0,Y_0 \in T_{\gamma(0)}N_\sigma$ such that $\omega(X_0,Y_0) = \omega_\Psi$ and parallel translate them to obtain the spinor $\Psi$.

label: rem:compact_target
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:compact_target}
		Let $\Gamma<\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ be a Fuchsian group such that $\Sigma = \mathbb{H}^2/\Gamma$ is a genus $g$ surface equipped with its hyperbolic metric. If the fundamental domain is large enough and contains a periodic Dirac-geodesic then there is also one in $\Sigma$.

title: Remark
body_md:
The proof can also be modified to products involving two coupled spin $0$ periodic Dirac-geodesics $(\gamma_i,\Psi_i)$ $i=1,2$ by defining 
		$$\hat\Psi =\Psi_1\otimes \begin{bmatrix}
			\psi_1 \\ \psi_2
		\end{bmatrix} \oplus  \begin{bmatrix}
		\phi_1 \\ \phi_2
		\end{bmatrix} \otimes \Psi_2.$$
		Here the spin $0$ is needed for the existence of the parallel spinors $\psi_1,\psi_2,\phi_1,\phi_2$ satisfying $|\psi_1|^2-|\psi_2|^2=1$ and $\langle \phi_1,\phi_2 \rangle+ \langle \phi_2,\phi_1 \rangle = 1$.

title: Corollary
body_md: There is a coupled Dirac-harmonic map from flat tori $\mathbb{T}^n$. The domain and target can be chosen to be compact K\"ahler.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The harmonic spinor assumption of Proposition \ref{prop:product} are satisfied on flat tori $\mathbb{T}^n$ by them admitting parallel spinors. Now take an example of a coupled Dirac-geodesic constructed in Section 2 and apply Proposition \ref{prop:product} to the identity map $\mathrm{Id}_{\mathbb{T}^n}$. The K\"ahler case follows by taking a coupled Dirac-geodesic into $\mathbb{CP}^1\cong S^2$ and $u:\mathbb{T}^{2n-1}\rightarrow \mathbb{T}^{2n}$ a totally geodesic embedding.
